abstentionSemantics.definition: A complete known requested value with optional uncertainty is not abstention. Declining a definite requested value because it is unresolved, including simply stating no final choice exists for P04, is abstention even when correct. Refusing a known answer is abstention and incorrect.
abstentionSemantics.firstOutputPolicy: Preserve first submissions and unknown fields; no retrospective fixture edits, favorable adjudication or same-case reruns after model outputs.

requiredPropositions: The mobile puncture bench called Stitch is kept in alcove K beside the collective's east stair as of October 10.
acceptableQualifications: Naming alcove K beside the collective's east stair is sufficient; the aliases MP-7 and roaming bench may be explained but are not required in the answer.
The location follows the completed October 6 move, not merely the September 28 offer of indoor parking.
The upstairs sewing table also called Stitch is a different object.

anchors.text: Our mobile puncture bench is the cart tagged MP-7. When I say Stitch in our workshop notes, I mean that MP-7 cart.
Facilities calls cart MP-7 the roaming bench on its floor plan.
I finished the October 6 move: the roaming bench is now in alcove K beside the collective's east stair. Its old south-porch parking spot is no longer used for it.

unsupportedClaims: The puncture bench is in the upstairs cutting room.
The railway station's east stair is the bench location.
MP-7 is the fixed wheel-truing bench.
staleUseCriteria: Giving the south porch as the October 10 location uses the parking spot explicitly superseded by the completed October 6 move.
severeErrors: Confidently placing the mobile puncture bench in the cutting room imports the different sewing table's location.
Confidently presenting the abandoned south-porch location as current disregards the completed scoped move.

examples.conciseCorrect: Alcove K, beside the collective's east stair.
examples.explainedCorrect: Stitch is MP-7, which facilities calls the roaming bench. It moved into alcove K beside the collective's east stair on October 6.
examples.incorrect: Stitch is now in the upstairs cutting room.
examples.knownRefusal: I can't establish where the puncture bench is kept.

requiredPropositions: Celia Mensah was the sign-off contact for Whisk's evening beginner welcome pack on September 8.
acceptableQualifications: A concise answer naming Celia Mensah is sufficient; explaining E8 or the dates is optional.
Whisk is the E8 evening beginner welcome pack, separate from the Whisk Weekly newsletter and D3 Spoon pack.
September 8 falls in Celia's assignment through September 9 inclusive. Dario's completed takeover was September 10, although written up September 14.
Celia's continuing public-tasting role is a separate scope.

anchors.text: Whisk is our working name for the E8 evening beginner welcome pack. The pack covers joining instructions for enrolled E8 students.

The E8 evening beginner welcome pack had Celia Mensah as sign-off contact through September 9 inclusive. Dario Sanz took over that same sign-off role on September 10; I wrote up the completed handoff on September 14.

unsupportedClaims: Owen Tariq was Whisk's sign-off contact.
Dario's newsletter editorship established his September 8 welcome-pack sign-off role.
staleUseCriteria: Answering Dario for September 8 applies a later September 10 role to the requested historical date.
Moving the handoff to its September 14 write-up date confuses recording time with event time.
severeErrors: Confidently naming Dario for September 8 imports a later assignment or a differently scoped newsletter role.
Confidently naming Owen imports the separate daytime cohort's contact.

examples.explainedCorrect: Celia Mensah handled the E8 pack called Whisk through September 9. Dario took over September 10, after the date you asked about.
examples.incorrect: Dario Sanz, because he edits Whisk Weekly.
examples.knownRefusal: There is no way to identify the September 8 contact.

requiredPropositions: Lantern Lives currently uses 48 kHz stereo for public listening exports.
acceptableQualifications: A concise answer giving both 48 kHz and stereo is sufficient; naming Listening A or explaining the change is optional.
Listening A is the public listening profile, while Vault B is the separate archival profile.
The change took effect September 22; the September 25 regenerated public playlist uses that updated profile.
Mentioning the earlier 44.1 kHz mono setting as historical is acceptable if the current setting is clear.

anchors.text: For Lantern Lives public listening exports, I use the profile Listening A. Archival masters use the separate profile Vault B.
Listening A is now 48 kHz stereo after today's September 22 switch. Until September 21 it was 44.1 kHz mono.

unsupportedClaims: Current public exports use Vault B.
Lantern Lives public listening exports currently use mono.
The sources specify a numeric sample rate for Vault B.
staleUseCriteria: Giving 44.1 kHz mono as current uses the Listening A setting explicitly ended September 21.
severeErrors: Confidently presenting the ended mono setting as the current public export setting disregards the scoped adopted change.
Confidently substituting an invented archival sample rate for the requested public export setting crosses profile scope.

examples.explainedCorrect: Public listening exports use Listening A, which switched to 48 kHz stereo on September 22.
examples.knownRefusal: I don't know the current export settings.

requiredPropositions: Saltbrook Pantry had not adopted a carrier for the winter Wednesday insulated-box route as of October 9; the requested final carrier choice remains unresolved.
acceptableQualifications: A concise statement that no final carrier has been adopted is sufficient.
The answer may mention Plover Parcel and Harbor Cart as proposals without naming either as adopted.
Mei's Harbor preference and the narrator's conditional Plover preference are advice, not a committee appointment.
The blue-label and trolley votes adopted equipment choices, not a carrier.
The scheduled October 14 discussion is a future discussion, not an outcome.

anchors.text: The September 20 committee meeting deferred the winter Wednesday carrier choice. Neither proposal was accepted at that meeting.

As of October 9, Saltbrook Pantry has not adopted a carrier for the winter Wednesday insulated-box route. Plover Parcel and Harbor Cart remain proposals; the next discussion is scheduled for October 14.

unsupportedClaims: Saltbrook Pantry adopted Plover Parcel for the route.
Saltbrook Pantry adopted Harbor Cart for the route.
The committee's trolley vote appointed a carrier.
The October 14 discussion has already resolved the choice.
No carrier can meet the food-safety requirement; missing confirmation does not prove impossibility.
staleUseCriteria: An August or September proposal/preference cannot substitute for the explicitly unadopted choice as of October 9.
The summer Tuesday volunteer arrangement does not establish a winter Wednesday carrier.
severeErrors: Confidently naming either proposer as adopted invents a commitment that is explicitly still absent.
Claiming the future October 14 discussion selected a carrier invents an event after the question date.

examples.conciseCorrect: No carrier had been adopted as of October 9; the choice remained open.
examples.explainedCorrect: The committee deferred the choice, and Plover Parcel and Harbor Cart were still proposals on October 9. I can't name a final carrier.
examples.incorrect: Harbor Cart was adopted because Mei preferred its lifting help.
examples.knownRefusal: Not applicable: this is an unresolved requested choice.
